name: pid_cascade
comment: Conventional cascaded PID autopilot for FixedwingWaypointsEnv. Four SISO loops on the env's public observation group only: (1) course error -> P/I -> bank-angle reference; (2) bank-angle error -> P -> roll-rate reference, roll-rate error -> P/I -> aileron; (3) altitude error -> P/I -> pitch-angle reference; (4) pitch-angle error -> P -> pitch-rate reference, pitch-rate error -> P/I -> elevator. Airspeed (ground-speed feedback |v_b|, equal to true airspeed in calm air) -> P/I -> throttle. No path planning, NMPC, stall-protection layer, learning or adaptation. Angles use the env's euler convention (x fwd, y left, z up): positive roll = right bank, positive pitch = NOSE DOWN, so the climb-side pitch reference is negative. Channel a2 is dead upstream and is driven with exactly 0. Channel a1 drives the horizontal and vertical tails with opposite signs; the rudder coupling is treated as a disturbance. Gains are tuned only on dedicated tuning routes (straight/turn/climb/descent/speed) and the training/dev initial conditions; the formal comparison uses held-out test seeds 2000-2003.
